Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Optimize toolkit looks promising for our customer-facing embeddings and chat features. Procurement asked me to get a concrete pilot proposal that covers: pricing for a 90-day pilot, recommended quantization approach to shave costs, and any caching/batching guardrails we should apply in production.

Key constraints:
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for short chat flows (~64 tokens).
- Data: customer PII, need SOC2 evidence (we'll request separately).
- Pilot target: 500k tokens / month average, burst to 2M.

Could you share an initial packaging + discount proposal and a short tech note on quantization + caching tradeoffs we should expect? Also please attach any SKU/price sheet we can pass to procurement.

Appreciate it —
Elena

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary below and attached a SKU worksheet (Optimize_Toolkit_SKU_v3.pdf) and a lightweight TCO model for quantization choices.

Proposal (90-day pilot):
- Pilot credits: 30% credit on hosted token usage (applied to first 90 days), with a one-time $5k onboarding credit for integrator support.
- Pilot scope: up to 2M burst tokens / month; comfortable steady state 500k tokens/month.
- Technical guardrails: enable prefix KV caching for stable prompt prefixes, cap batch window at 10–15ms for p95 latency target.
- Upgrade path: annual committed credits receive 45% credit + reserved throughput pricing and SLA.

Quantization recommendation (short):
- If you can tolerate modest quality delta on some system prompts, 4-bit quantization (Q4_0 or Q4_K_M) provides ~2–2.5x cost reduction on GPU memory and 20–35% per-token cost drop on our hosted stack versus fp16 inference for large decoder models.
- For chat with short sequences (<=128 tokens) we recommend Q4 with KV cache enabled; it preserves runtime latency and keeps memory local.
- Risks: edge-case hallucination sensitivity may increase for very small context windows — include evals on your critical prompt set.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, we'll draft a short SOW and a pilot Order Form (DocuSign).
2) Marcus will drop a one-page tech note that maps quantization choices to expected cost/latency for your workload.

I'll follow up with Marcus and Lauren on the SOW cadence.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Elena / Soojin — adding the technical mapping you asked for. Short tech note below (pulled from our internal runbook).

— Tech note: quantization + caching practicals —
1) Latency vs cost trade: Q4 quant yields lower memory pressure (more tokens per GPU) but adds a ~5–12% decode overhead per-token versus fp16 on some kernels. With continuous batching disabled for strict latency, expect p95 delta of ~+10–40ms depending on model. Given your 250ms p95 target at 64 tokens, Q4 + small batching (batch window 5–15ms) + KV caching should keep you under SLO for most traffic shapes.

2) Caching guidance: enable prefix/KV caching for shared system prompts and initial context like user profiles. For chat flows with short user turns, prefix caching reduces repeated attention compute significantly (we've measured 30–50% CPU/GPU cost drop for stable prefixes).

3) Autoscaling and throttling: configure a conservative burst policy (2x steady) with token-based throttles; for the pilot we can surface recommended thresholds in the Console to avoid cold-start latency.

4) Quality guardrails: run a 1000-prompt eval set across your top 10 intents in both fp16 and Q4; we can help automate and store diffs in the Console for regression alerts.

If you want, I can run the eval using a 1k prompt sample and return an A/B report (expected turnaround 48 hours).

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
